instructions: Cut the rind off the fontina if it has one, then cut it into 1/2 inch cubes.
Bring 4 cups of water and the salt to a boil in a large heavy pot over high heat.

Turn the heat to medium-low. Pour in the polenta in a thin stream, whisking as you go. Switch to a wooden spoon and stir for 5 minutes, until it's thick and pulls away from the sides of the pot. Check your package, as the time can differ a little.
Stir in the milk until the polenta is smooth and loose again, about 1 minute. If it's too stiff, add a splash of water.
Take the pot off the heat. Add the fontina and 4 tbsp of the butter, and stir until both have melted.
Melt the remaining 2 tbsp butter in a small pan over medium heat for about 2 minutes, until it foams.
Taste the polenta. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. Spoon it into warm bowls, drizzle with the melted butter and finish with the pepper.
method_notes: Every version cooks polenta in salted water, loosens it with milk, and stirs in fontina and butter, with a little melted butter over the top. The lead simmers regular polenta for 45 minutes; this uses quick-cooking polenta so it fits a weeknight, and the second version says that works too. Stir the cheese in off the heat so it doesn't go stringy. Amounts are scaled up for 4 as a dinner.
